lesson.name: Learn The Bogo Indian Defense
lesson.description: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 Bb4+ leads to the strategically rich Bogo Indian Defense. Learn the key ideas and tactics for both sides.

{What powerful pawn sacrifice did GM Boris Gelfand play to break apart Black's
pawn structure?} 12. d5 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look
for a useful pawn break.] [%hint Sacrifice your d-pawn to block the b7-bishop.]
} (12. Bb2 $5 {This is a good choice, but GM Gelfand preferred a powerful pawn
break. What did he play?}) (12. Ne1 $5 {This is a good choice, but GM Gelfand
preferred a powerful pawn break. What did he play?}) (12. Rb1 $5 {This is a
good choice, but GM Gelfand preferred a powerful pawn break. What did he play?}
) (12. Nd2 $5 {This is a good choice, but GM Gelfand preferred a powerful pawn
break. What did he play?}) (12. c5 $2 Bd5 {White's dark-squared bishop is
somewhat restricted in this pawn structure. Try again and look for a better
pawn break.}) 12... exd5 {Good start! White can recapture right away, but it's
stronger to threaten a fork to win material. How should you do it?} 13. Nd4 {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a way to threaten a
powerful knight fork.] [%hint Centralize your knight.] Well done! The knight
heads to e6 if Black can't stop it. Meanwhile, the c1-bishop will soon dominate
the long diagonal from b2. In the real game, Black declined the sacrifice and
met d5 with e6-e5. We will examine a key moment in that game in the next
challenge.} (13. cxd5 $2 Bxd5 {White has good compensation for the sacrificed
pawn, but it's stronger to threaten a fork before recapturing. How should you
do it?}) *

{How did Gelfand attempt to break open the center to benefit from the bishop
pair?} 15. f4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a
powerful pawn break.] [%hint Target e5 with a pawn.]} (15. c5 $2 Bxd5 {Black is
happy to accept this pawn sacrifice. Try again and look for a stronger pawn
break.}) (15. e4 $2 fxe4 {Black doesn't mind opening the f-file. Try again and
look for a stronger pawn break.}) (15. g3 $2 Qf6 {This is playable, but it's
stronger to fight for the central dark-squares with a pawn. How should you do
it?}) (15. f3 $5 {This is OK, but there's an even better move with the f-pawn.
Try to find it.}) 15... Rae8 {Black doesn't want to open the long dark
diagonal for White's bishop, but Gelfand forces a weakening with his next move.
What strong threat did he find?} 16. Bd3 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try
again and look for a useful threat.] [%hint Make a battery on the b1-h7
diagonal.] Good work! Black shut down the immediate threat with e5-e4, but
then White was able to dominate the long dark diagonal and win a great
game in Gelfand - Tomashevsky, 2014.} (16. Qa4 $5 {This fork wins a pawn and
White should be doing well, but it can be risky to bring the queen so far away
from the kingside. Try to find Gelfand's strong threat to the f5-pawn.}) (16.
fxe5 $2 Nxe5 {The knight is well-placed on e5. Try again and look for a better
way to add pressure against the f5-pawn.}) *

{How did GM Magnus Carlsen fight for the center and reach a safe position?} 
11... dxc4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a good
capture.] [%hint Trade pawns.]} (11... c5 $2 12. cxd5 {Black will have to
defend a tough position with an isolated d-pawn. Try again and look for a
better pawn move.}) (11... e5 $2 12. cxd5 {White wins a pawn. Try again and
look for a stronger pawn move.}) 12. Bxc4 {White must move the bishop a second
time in the opening in order to recapture. How should Black break apart the
white pawn center?} c5 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for
a strong pawn break.] [%hint Target the d4-pawn.] Well done! Carlsen drew
relatively easily from here against GM Levon Aronian on his way to winning the
2013 Candidates Tournament.} (12... b6 $5 {This is OK, but GM Carlsen
preferred to contest the center with a pawn. How did he do it?}) (12... b5 $5 {
This is OK, but GM Carlsen preferred to contest the center with a pawn. How
did he do it?}) (12... e5 $2 13. Ng5 {Black has difficulties defending the
f7-pawn. Try again and look for a stronger pawn break.}) *

{How should Black save the c6-knight?} 10... Nb8 {[%wrong White wins material.
Try again and look for a good way to save your knight.] [%hint Retreat your
knight all the way home.]} (10... Nd8 $2 11. b4 {The knight has no safe moves
from d8. Try again and look for a stronger knight retreat.}) (10... Nd4 $2 11.
Nxd4 {White will soon win a pawn. Try again and look for a stronger knight
move.}) (10... Nb4 $2 11. a3 {The knight must retreat and block the a7-pawn.
Try again and look for a better knight move.}) (10... Na5 $2 11. b4 {The
knight is trapped. Try again and look for a better knight move.}) 11. b4 {
In this closed position, Black has time to redeploy the knight, but first, it's
useful to play a strong pawn break. Try to find a good one.} a5 {[%wrong
There's a better move. Try again and look for a strong pawn break.] [%hint
Offer a trade for the b4-pawn and aim to open the a-file for your rook.] Well
played! Black went on to score a solid draw in Hakobyan - Perelshteyn, 2018.} (
11... Bg4 $5 {This is OK, but there's a pawn break on the queenside that's
stronger. Try to find it.}) (11... c6 $2 12. c5 {White opens the center with a
good position. Try again and look for a better queenside pawn break.}) *

{How should White handle the threat against b4?} 12. a3 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for a precise way to protect your b-pawn.] 
[%hint Defend b4 with another pawn.] Good work! White can set up the c4-c5

an advantage with the queenside so blocked. Try again and look for a better
way to defend your b-pawn.}) (12. Rb1 $2 axb4 {Black attacks a2 and wins a

{What useful threat can Black play to obtain a comfortable position?} 7... Ne4
{[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a strong threat.]

good winning chances. Try again and look for a strong threat.}) (7... O-O $2 8.
O-O {White has more space and good winning chances. Try again and look for a
strong threat.}) (7... Qb4 $2 8. Qc3 {Even after a queen trade, White has a
small advantage. Try again and look for a better way to target White's queen.})
8. Qc2 {The e4-knight is in danger, but there's no need to retreat. How should
you keep fighting for the initiative?} Qb4+ {[%wrong There's a better move.
Try again and look for a good check.] [%hint Find a good check.]} 9. Nc3 {

the white structure after Nc3?} Nxc3 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again
and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Trade knights.]} 10. Qxc3 {Good idea!
How can you force White to accept doubled pawns?} Qxc3+ {[%wrong White is
doing well. Try again and look for a good capture.] [%hint Trade queens.] Well
done! White must accept doubled pawns in the endgame and fight for a draw.} *
